title: JudgeBench
evidenceStatus: 100 sampled pairs; 200/200 completed orientations; full candidate texts verified against pinned upstream; 14 transport failures recovered
summary: The current 77% headline measures ordered decisions, while official JudgeBench two-order scoring gives 63% on the same 100 pairs. Full candidate visibility and recovery are working; the next work is complete 620-pair coverage, comparable scoring, and an interaction that makes order-sensitive failures inspectable.
strengths: All 200 published rows include full questions and candidate strings, with zero discrepancies against pinned upstream.
Recovered only transport failures; completed predictions were retained.
React separates returned-answer accuracy from availability and lets visitors vote before revealing judgments.

findings.title: Ordered accuracy differs from official JudgeBench score
findings.evidence: src/jev_lab/benchmarks.py:153; experience-prototypes/scripts/metrics.py:18; probe: 63 both-correct, 28 inconsistent, 9 both-wrong pairs
findings.impact: 77% ordered accuracy is not comparable to the official two-order score, which is 63%.
findings.fix: Lead with upstream-compatible two-order score; retain ordered accuracy, completion and tie counts as separate diagnostics; add official-rule test vectors.

findings.title: Sample changes benchmark composition and overstates independent units
findings.evidence: src/jev_lab/data.py:101; 100/620 pairs, 50 per response model; 82% MMLU versus 49.68% full; 83 distinct source questions
findings.impact: The sample does not estimate the official release distribution directly; repeated orientations and source questions inflate apparent sample size.
findings.fix: Evaluate all 350 GPT and 270 Claude pairs; report split/source scores and cluster intervals by source plus original question ID.

findings.title: Order sensitivity is a number rather than an inspectable intervention
findings.evidence: experience-prototypes/src/benchmarks.tsx:25,98; 200 orientation rows navigated separately; pair 88c03f19-2b85-5b04-b0f8-42e9a765098e selects displayed B both ways
findings.impact: Visitors cannot naturally compare the 28 pairs whose underlying winner changes after swapping.
findings.fix: Navigate unique pairs, add controlled swap, preserve canonical answer identity and show both judgments together with disagreement filters.

findings.title: Atomic scoring is whole-answer shared-context scoring with positional tie-breaking
findings.evidence: src/jev_lab/benchmarks.py:124; five equal-score cases assigned A; 71.5% ordered accuracy and 51% official two-order score
findings.impact: The label suggests finer or independent verification than performed, and ties acquire arbitrary positional winners.
findings.fix: Rename the method, preserve ties, show the negative ablation, and compare isolated-answer scoring before proposing claim-level checks.

findings.title: Difficult-case reading and blind voting remain limited
findings.evidence: experience-prototypes/src/benchmarks.tsx:29,158,163; src/style.css:2140; candidate markup is plain text in 420px scroll regions
findings.impact: Math/code is harder to read; mistakes filtering and target search leak information before voting; no durable first vote exists.
findings.fix: Separate blind practice and diagnostics; add safe Markdown/math, expanded/raw reading, explicit reveal, first-vote persistence and pair deep links.

simulation.title: The order-sensitivity courtroom
simulation.description: Read and vote on a unique pair, reveal gold and both Jev orientations, then swap seats while answer identities stay fixed. Compare pairwise, whole-answer and consensus methods, filter disagreements and export exact evidence. Optional live votes are exploratory records and cannot overwrite the frozen benchmark.
simulation.jevsRole: Return defined pairwise or answer-correctness judgments without access to dataset labels.
simulation.codeRole: Keep labels hidden, map canonical candidates through swaps, score with the official rule, render safely, preserve human votes, expose unavailable requests and export provenance.
acceptanceCriteria: All 620 pairs have complete byte-verified raw text in both orientations.
Swapping twice restores candidate identities; both recorded judgments are available after reveal.
Blind mode hides gold, model votes and diagnostic filters until the first vote is fixed.
All headline metrics exactly reproduce from exported evidence and distinguish pairs from orientations.
Cancelled or unavailable live votes never alter benchmark scores.
Keyboard and dark/light reading flows support expanded math/code and raw-text views.

evaluation.design: Freeze the protocol, evaluate all 620 pairs in both orders across three scheduling seeds 42/43/44: 3720 state requests and 11160 decision questions before retries. Reproduce official two-order scoring and use 10000 source-question-cluster bootstrap resamples for paired comparisons; report run variability separately. No benchmark labels enter prompts or tuning. Isolated-answer ablation costs 1240 additional requests per pass.
baselines: Always displayed A: 0% official / 50% ordered expected
Independent random votes: 25% official / 50% ordered expected
Canonical random answer across swaps: 50% expected
metrics: Official two-order score per response-model split and source family
Order disagreement and correct/tied/incorrect pair counts

coverage.current: 100/620 unique response pairs (16.13%), 50 GPT and 50 Claude; 200 completed orientations; 83 distinct source questions.
coverage.full: Official gpt split 350 pairs and claude split 270 pairs; 620 total, 1240 orientations; 268 distinct (source, original_id) questions in pinned release.
coverage.feasibility: Full pass needs 1240 API state requests, 3720 questions with existing contract. Cached source is available; maximum serialized state 9,172 bytes. No candidate-generation calls needed. Tokenizer preflight and provider rate-limit recovery remain practical checks; no evident data-size blocker.

libraries.name: SciPy bootstrap
libraries.use: Compute reproducible uncertainty after grouping dependent records by original source question.

libraries.name: react-markdown
libraries.use: Safe candidate Markdown rendering with documented math-plugin integration and a raw-text toggle; no raw HTML or code execution.
